issue_reference: Assigned in the registration pull request rather than guessed in advance.
purpose: This is the production training run whose output is submitted to the tournament. It is not a screen: its job is to train the agent for as long as the remaining budget allows and to retain the trajectory so the shipped policy can be chosen from it. A comparison is registered alongside because the budget supports two arms and an unregistered single-configuration run would make no testable claim.
hypothesis: Every completed Task 4 screen trained for at most 2,400 episodes, and the retained trajectory over 600, 1,200, 1,800 and 2,400 episodes showed no score trend while self-kills fell and survival rose. Whether score responds to a budget an order of magnitude larger is untested, and no result in this project licenses extrapolating the flat range to 30,000 episodes. This run trains twelve and a half times longer than the largest screen and retains a checkpoint every 2,000 episodes, so the budget response is measured rather than assumed. The registered factor is the learning rate: 0.0002 is the only dose that beat the incumbent while holding all three retention gates, and 0.0001 tests whether a smaller step is better suited to a long run, where the dose that wins over 400 episodes need not be the dose that wins over 30,000. Training is sequential, so a milestone at episode N is exactly the agent N episodes would have produced; a long run therefore contains every shorter run as a prefix and costs nothing relative to one, provided the trajectory is retained and selection may read it.

prior_evidence.trainable_scope: Lifting the Task 3 freeze beat the frozen regime by 1.429 score, interval [0.888, 1.996]; training under the frozen scope was worse than not training. Every arm here registers all_weights and the frozen regime is not carried.
prior_evidence.learning_rate: The dose ladder at 400 episodes gave 0.0002 a gain of 0.708 over the unchanged incumbent, interval [0.175, 1.279], and it was the only dose holding all three retention gates. 0.0005 lost two and 0.00005 lost all three while gaining least. The control arm here is that winning dose.
prior_evidence.random_episode_period: Periods of 5, 10 and 20 all beat the incumbent and the response was monotone in favour of the shortest period; less random play was worse. Period 5 is registered for both arms. Whether a period that lengthens late would beat a constant one over 30,000 episodes was never tested.
prior_evidence.training_opponents: The mixed line-up passed all three retention gates where the hard line-up failed all three, and once the rate was corrected to 0.0002 no measurable tournament difference between line-ups remained. The mixed line-up is registered for both arms.
prior_evidence.replay_capacity: A tenfold range produced no detected effect and none was excluded; the interval was wide and spanned zero. Capacity stays at its inherited value.
prior_evidence.kill_reward: Raising the kill reward tenfold, which aligns the agent's internal ratio with the tournament's coins + 5 x kills, left eliminations flat at 0.094 / 0.094 / 0.081 and lowered score monotonically. The native reward is registered unchanged.
prior_evidence.power: The unchanged incumbent scored between 1.375 and 3.100 across seven independent forty-world sets. No absolute score is comparable across runs. Every contrast drawn here is paired on shared worlds within this run.
prior_evidence.reference_implementation: rule_based_agent against three copies of itself over forty games scores 3.17 with 0.188 eliminations and 0.544 self-kills per game, and never survives a round. Trained agents in this project reach 0.08-0.15 eliminations while surviving 0.25-0.47 of their rounds, so the elimination rate is near the hand-written reference rather than near zero.

intervention.baseline_shared_by_every_arm: the Task 3 candidate as the starting point, the all_weights trainable scope, native rewards with no approach shaping, one optimizer update per eligible transition, the mixed training line-up and a random-episode period of five
intervention.persistence: training-only; evaluation loads the unchanged archived agent
intervention.registered_risk: No run in this project has trained past 2,400 episodes. The resume machinery is proven at 1,375 episodes, not at 30,000, and the exploration schedule was chosen on 1,200-episode evidence. Divergence, retention collapse or a score that decays late are all possible and none would be detectable from the screens already completed. Milestones every 2,000 episodes exist so that any of these is recoverable by selecting an earlier point on the trajectory rather than by discarding the run.
intervention.milestone_evaluation: Milestones are evaluated during the run on the development suite only, to monitor the trajectory and to inform the choice of selected checkpoint. The held-out suite is not read during monitoring.

random_episode_schedule: Per arm: for each block of `random_episode_period` episodes, random.Random(agent_seed + 168000000 + block_index).randrange(period) selects one fully random episode and the rest are greedy.

classic-rule-based.role: development; every registered gate and the selection contrast read this suite

holdout-rule-based.role: held out; forty worlds disjoint from every other suite and from every earlier registration. No gate, no selection step and no monitoring decision may read this suite. It is reported once, for the artifact selection has already chosen, so the number quoted in the report is not the number the artifact was picked for.

primary_endpoint: Mean native score per game on classic-rule-based against the unchanged reference. Tournament placing is decided by score, which is coins plus five times eliminations.

uncertainty.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap over replicas and shared worlds
uncertainty.family: one test family per arm judged under the corrected rule, the control included; the promotion rule is conjunctive, so only the arm count is Bonferroni-adjusted
uncertainty.role: registered decision input, not a post-hoc description

selection: An arm is promotable only if every applicable integrity gate, every retention gate and every efficacy gate passes. Among promotable arms the largest mean score gain over the unchanged reference is chosen, and within it the median-final replica by that score; the best-looking replica is not selectable. If no arm is promotable, the shipped checkpoint is chosen descriptively from the retained trajectory on the development suite and the report states plainly that it passed no prospective gate, following the precedent already recorded for the Task 3 incumbent. Either way the held-out suite is read once, after the artifact is fixed.
scientific_gates: Original cumulative Task 1/2/3 requirements are unchanged; this run cannot retrospectively establish any of them.
known_gate_defect: Judged under promotion rule version 2: the invalid-action gate compares each trained artifact against the unchanged reference rather than demanding a global zero the reference itself cannot reach, frozen_online_weights reports not-applicable for arms registered to move the weights, and promotion and selection key on score, the registered primary endpoint.

machine_allocation.training: 6 concurrent workers, one torch thread each
machine_allocation.latency: one worker on an otherwise idle machine; the only latency source
